      "source_quote": "The concept of quantum nanolaminates (QNL) postulates the decoupling of band gap and refractive index... We will show that the quantization effect can be observed in nanolaminate structures of the material combinations Ta2O5-SiO2... Furthermore, the use of the QNL as the high refractive index material in optical interference coatings was successfully demonstrated in anti-reflection and long pass filter coatings.",

      "physical_effect": "Decoupling of band gap and refractive index; successful demonstration in AR coatings.",
      "conditions_and_unknowns": [
        "Abstract does not specify layer count, thickness bounds, or specific telecom wavelengths.",
        "Mechanism relies on sub-nanometer quantization effects not explicitly detailed in snippet."
      ],
      "goal_ids": ["G1", "G2"],
      "inference_bridge": "Hypothesize that treating Ta2O5/SiO2 pairs as effective medium layers or using very thin alternating stacks could provide tailored effective indices for dual-band matching, transferring the 'decoupling' concept to macroscopic thickness optimization within the 20-400 nm constraint."
    },
    {
      "id": "D2",
      "evidence_id": "E_a2c307eafcd3d4b2c13a30feafa915e25383e472cd210698cce20b43ae9d2de1",
      "source_quote": "To attain the desired anti-reflection outcome... it is necessary for the reflected beam's amplitude at both the air-coating interface and the coating-substrate interface to be identical and precisely out of phase by one-half wave (180 • )...       "physical_effect": "Destructive interference via amplitude matching and 180-degree phase shift.",
      "conditions_and_unknowns": [
        "Snippet targets 400-800 nm (visible), not telecom bands.",

        "Specific 'half-wave' layer role in broadening bandwidth is implied but not numerically proven for dual disjoint bands."
      ],

      "inference_bridge": "Transfer the 'quarter-half-quarter' concept to Ta2O5/SiO2 stacks at telecom wavelengths.       "source_quote": "When the thickness of the anti-reflection coating satisfies the quarter-wave condition, destructive interference of reflected waves occurs, which minimizes the overall reflection of incident radiation. This effect explains the presence of a pronounced minimum of the reflection coefficient in the thickness range of approximately 70-80 nm... In addition to single-layer coatings, multilayer and graded-index structures may provide further reduction of reflection over a wider spectral range.",

      "physical_effect": "Destructive interference at specific thickness; broader reduction via graded index.",
      "conditions_and_unknowns": [
        "Snippet discusses single-layer minima (70-80 nm) likely for visible/NIR.",
        "Graded-index mention is qualitative; no specific discrete layer approximation provided."
      ],

      "inference_bridge": "Hypothesize that approximating a graded index profile using a discrete staircase of Ta2O5/SiO2 layers (changing thickness or material fraction per layer) can broaden the low-reflection zone to encompass both target bands, compared to a simple quarter-wave stack."

    }
